plan: [This is a common-value auction with winner’s curse. My signal is 24; unconditional E[common|signal=24]=24.5, but conditioning on being the highest (beating two rivals) reduces the expected common value. Solving for E[common | my signal=24 and others’ signals ≤24] gives ≈23.82. In a symmetric equilibrium of the second-price auction I should bid that conditional expectation. I therefore shade slightly below my signal to avoid the winner’s curse.]

[Compute posterior for the common value given my signal S=37. Noise is uniform on [-20,20], so likelihood is constant over C∈[20,29]; posterior is uniform on [20,29]. Thus E[C|S]= (20+29)/2 = 24.5. In a second-price auction, bidding my conditional expectation (24.5) is the optimal strategy to maximize expected profit and avoid the winner’s curse.]

[Compute posterior E[common value | signal=10]. Prior C~Uniform[20,29], noise U~Uniform[-20,20]. For S=10 all C in [20,29] are feasible, so posterior is uniform on [20,29] and E[C|S=10]=24.5. In a second-price auction bidding your conditional expectation is the Bayes–Nash equilibrium and mitigates the winner's curse. Thus I will bid 24.5.]
